Unit Personality -> Preferences: static decompilation of both configured PE images

Reference image PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
  producer RVA 47f680..481e13 (code), 481e14..481efe (embedded tables)
Classic image PE:6a70b91c:0270a000

  Every producer instruction/table RVA below uses the reference coordinate;
  classic coordinate = reference coordinate - 2440.

PAGE DISPATCH, 47f721..47f745
  switch (sheet.int32_at_1a8c) {
    0: ->481630: traits/general personality, alcohol/outdoors/tragedy prose;
    1: ->481583: values via e248a0;
    2: ->4800b2: Preferences, decompiled in full below;
    3: ->47f74b: needs summary and 30 need types;
    default: return with cleared source/box vectors.
  }
  Traits, values, and needs text in this shared function are not reachable from
  Preferences selector 2. Native-literal-scopes.tsv explicitly distinguishes them.

PAGE STORAGE, 47f6b6..47f721
  sheet+1a90 = vector<string*> personality_raw_str;
  sheet+1aa8 = vector<textbox*> personality_text_boxes;
  sheet+1ac0 = cached wrapping width, cleared to zero.
  Existing raw strings and boxes are discarded before any page is rebuilt.

PREFERENCE RECORD, as read by native producer
  +00 int16 type
  +04 int32 subject (item kind / creature / plant / color / shape / art form ID)
  +08 int32 item_subtype (item calls consume its low int16)
  +0c int32 material_type (material calls consume its low int16)
  +10 int32 material_index
  +14 int16 matter_state
  +16 uint8 flags; bit 0 is visible
  +18 int32 prefstring_seed
  unit+12e uint8 sex: 0 female, 1 male, other neuter
  unit+a98 = soul; soul+230..238 = vector<unit_preference*>.

COMPLETE PREFERENCES PRODUCTION, 4800b2..48157e
  if (!unit.soul || unit.soul.preferences.empty()) return;  // 4800d7..480102
  out = "[C:7:0:1]";                                     // 480151

  likes = preferences whose visible bit is set and type != 2 and type != 3;
  if (!likes.empty()) {
    name = "";
    pointer = current_unit_identity_name(unit);             // 13e5a90 at 4801f1
    if (pointer && pointer.byte_at_72 != 0)
      name = unit_name(pointer);                            // a94030 at 48020b
    out += name + " likes ";                              // 480223
    for (preference p : likes, preserving native vector order) {
      switch (p.type) {                                    // table 481e8c, 12 entries
        0:  // LikeMaterial; 480271
          out += material_name(p.material_type, p.material_index,
                               generic_flags=0, adjective=false,
                               matter_state=p.matter_state);
          if (p.matter_state == 0 && 419 <= p.material_type &&
              p.material_type <= 618) {
            if (material_has_flag(23,p.material_type,p.material_index))
              out += " wood";                            // 48031e
            else if (material_has_flag(24,p.material_type,p.material_index))
              out += " fabric";                          // 480357
          }
          break;
        1:  // LikeCreature; 480596
          out += creature_plural(int16(p.subject),caste=-1);
          out += " for their ";                          // 4805e1
          out += creature_prefstring(int16(p.subject),p.prefstring_seed);
          break;
        2: case 3: break; // filtered out before switch, targets 48086a
        4:  // LikeItem; 480370
          out += item_name(int16(p.subject),int16(p.item_subtype),
                           material_type=-1,material_index=-1,
                           flags=0,plural=true);
          break;
        5:  // LikePlant; 480402
        6:  // LikeTree; 4804cc; deliberately identical to LikePlant
          out += plant_name(p.subject,capitalize=false,plural=true);
          out += " for their ";                          // 480452 or 48051c
          out += plant_prefstring(p.subject,p.prefstring_seed);
          break;
        7:  // LikeColor; 48065c
          out += "the color " + color_name(int16(p.subject));
          break;
        8:  // LikeShape; 4806bf, no "the shape" prefix in native producer
          out += shape_name(int16(p.subject),plural=true);
          break;
        9:  // LikePoeticForm; 480712
        10: // LikeMusicalForm; 480786
        11: // LikeDanceForm; 4807f7
          form = lookup_by_id(selected_form_collection,p.subject);
          if (form && form.byte_at_7a != 0) {
            out += type==9 ? "the words of " : type==10 ? "the sound of "
                                                            : "the sight of ";
            out += generated_english_name(form+8,capitalize=true,shorten=false);
          }
          // Missing/unnamed forms emit no body, but still consume the counted
          // item and append the same list separator.
          break;
        default: break; // out-of-range types emit no body, still counted
      }
      append_list_separator(out, --remaining_likes);       // 48086a..480893
    }
  }

  foods = visible preferences with type==2;                 // 4808d6..480935
  if (!foods.empty()) {
    // Native uses lowercase here: it does not call a capitalizing pronoun
    // helper. The "e" operands in native-literals.tsv are suffix-copy
    // instructions belonging to "she", never independent pronouns.
    pronoun = unit.sex==1 ? "he" : unit.sex==0 ? "she" : "it";
    out += "When possible, " + pronoun + " prefers to consume ";
    for (preference p : foods, preserving native vector order) {
      switch (p.subject) { // remap byte table 481ee4 -> RVA table 481ebc
        48: // MEAT; 480af2
          food = creature_name_singular(int16(p.material_index));
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown meat";
          break;
        49: // FISH; 480b7b
          food = creature_name_singular(int16(p.material_type));
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown fish";
          break;
        54: // PLANT; 480c04
          food = plant_name_plural(p.material_index);
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown plants";
          break;
        69: // DRINK; 480c7d
          food = item_name(69,-1,p.material_type,p.material_index,plural=true);
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown drink";
          break;
        73: // LIQUID_MISC; 480cef
          food = item_name(73,-1,p.material_type,p.material_index,plural=true);
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown liquid";
          break;
        53: // SEEDS; 480d61
          food = item_name(53,-1,p.material_type,p.material_index,plural=true);
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown seeds";
          break;
        56: // PLANT_GROWTH; 480dd3
          food = item_name(56,p.item_subtype,p.material_type,p.material_index,plural=true);
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown leaves";
          break;
        70: // POWDER_MISC; 480e46
          food = item_name(70,-1,p.material_type,p.material_index,plural=true);
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown powder";
          break;
        71: // CHEESE; 480eb8
          food = item_name(71,-1,p.material_type,p.material_index,plural=true);
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown cheese";
          break;
        default: // All other values, including 50..52,55,57..68,72; 480f2a
          food = item_name(int16(p.subject),p.item_subtype,
                           p.material_type,p.material_index,plural=true);
          if (food.empty()) food="unknown item";
          break;
      }
      out += food;
      append_list_separator(out,--remaining_foods);         // 48109f..4810df
    }
  }

  hated = visible preferences with type==3;                 // 48117a..4811d4
  if (!hated.empty()) {
    pronoun = unit.sex==1 ? "He" : unit.sex==0 ? "She" : "It";
    out += pronoun + " absolutely detests ";               // 4812d6
    for (preference p : hated, preserving native vector order) {
      out += creature_name_plural(int16(p.subject));        // RAW+40 at 48138f
      // Invalid/negative creature ID -> empty; no "unknown creature" fallback.
      append_list_separator(out,--remaining_hated);         // 4813e9..481426
    }
  }

  // All three groups are independent. The seven nonempty subsets appear in
  // the order likes, foods, hated. No sentence is required as a leading group.
  // Nonempty preferences containing only invisible records still yield a
  // color-tag-only source string; there is no textual "no preferences" branch.
  if (!out.empty()) {
    sheet.personality_raw_str.push_back(copy(out));         // 481500..48152b
    sheet.personality_text_boxes.push_back(new_box(76));     // 481539..48156c
  }

APPEND_LIST_SEPARATOR(out, remaining), ALL THREE GROUPS
  if (remaining > 1) out += ", ";
  else if (remaining == 1) out += " and ";
  else out += ".  "; // Period plus two spaces. No Oxford comma is added.
  A single object NAME, PREFSTRING or generated form title may itself contain
  commas, conjunctions, apostrophes or punctuation. They remain one semantic
  field. Native list construction does not tokenize their contents.

DYNAMIC RAW FIELD HELPERS
  plant-name: reference 144d90, classic 144d20
    negative/out-of-range ID -> no body; plural=true selects RAW+70 NAME:PLURAL.
  creature-plural: reference aa3bd0, classic aa0c50
    caste=-1 and plural=true selects CREATURE_RAW+40 NAME:PLURAL;
    negative/out-of-range ID -> empty.
  color-name: reference 420fc0, classic 41eb80
    descriptor_color+50 NAME; low signed int16 ID; invalid -> empty.
  shape-plural: reference 1437f0, classic 143780
    descriptor_shape+70 NAME:PLURAL; low signed int16 ID; invalid -> empty.
  plant-prefstring: reference e35d60, classic e30cd0
    plant RAW vector+288..290; invalid index or empty vector -> empty.
  creature-prefstring: reference e35c70, classic e30be0
    creature RAW vector+148..150; invalid index or empty vector -> empty.
  Both prefstring helpers use this exact seed selection (64-bit wrap arithmetic):
    x = uint32(prefstring_seed) + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15;
    x = (x ^ (x >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9;
    x = (x ^ (x >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111eb;
    selected_index = (uint32(x >> 63) ^ uint32(x >> 32)) % vector.size();
    result = *vector[selected_index];
  No finite reason list is hardcoded in either helper: every RAW PREFSTRING is
  eligible, including modded entries; source-field translations must preserve
  the whole selected phrase.
  material-state-name: reference 14d1920, classic 14cc890
    Preferences passes generic_flags=0 and adjective=false, bypassing generic
    plant/yarn/cloth/etc flags. Result is optional historical-owner possessive,
    optional material prefix+520 and space, then STATE_NAME[state] at +b8+0x20*state.
    Invalid material -> "unknown material". All matter states flow through.
  item-name: reference a82c10..a880de, classic a7fc90..a8515e
    Complete code and all 93 main selector entries retained; flags/arguments
    are those shown at the Preferences calls. Subtyped RAW item NAME:PLURAL,
    adjective+plural, instrument names, plant-growth names and default nouns
    are all eligible. Shared source catalog is tools/extract_item_description_catalog.py
    and data/extracted/item-description-sources.tsv; its broader option branches should not
    be described as independent Preferences sentence families.
  unit-name: reference a94030, classic a910b0
  generated-art-form-name: reference a946e0, classic a91760
    Unit, civilization/form language words and authored names are dynamic data;
    static native extraction describes construction but cannot enumerate every
    generated or user-authored string.

COMPLETE GENERATED ART-FORM NAME FIELD GRAMMAR
  English formatter a946e0..a94ea2; classic a91760..a91f22.
  English-formatter instruction classic RVA = reference RVA - 2f80.
  Preferences sets capitalize=true, shorten=false at 48075b..480768,
  4807cf..4807dc and 480838..480845 (classic subtract 2440).
  This formatter always reads English WORD forms. Its two boolean arguments
  control capitalization and abbreviation, not English/local-language choice.

  language_name layout used by the formatter:
    +00 string first_name; +20 string authored nickname; +30 nickname length
    +40 int32 FrontCompound WORD; +44 int32 RearCompound WORD
    +48 int32 FirstAdjective WORD; +4c int32 SecondAdjective WORD
    +50 int32 HyphenCompound WORD; +54 int32 TheX WORD; +58 int32 OfX WORD
    +5c..68 int16 part_of_speech[7], corresponding to WORD fields above
    +6c int32 language ID; +72 bool has_name
  if (!name.has_name) return without changing the supplied output; a94723.
  Otherwise clear output; a94747.
  mode = 0;
  if (0 <= current_game_type && current_game_type <= 10)
    mode = nickname_display[current_game_type]; a94730..a94743.
  Native d_init modes are 0 REPLACE_FIRST, 1 CENTRALIZE, 2 REPLACE_ALL.

  quoted_nickname = char(0x60) + authored_nickname_bytes + char(0x27);
  // These are a backtick and an apostrophe, not matching apostrophe quotes.
  // The nickname's contents are copied verbatim; capitalization is not applied.
  if (!nickname.empty() && (mode==0 || mode==2)) {
    out = quoted_nickname; a94770..a947a9;
  } else {
    out = capitalize ? titlecase(first_name) : first_name; a947ae..a94879;
  }
  if (!nickname.empty() && mode==1) {
    if (!out.empty()) out += " "; a94899..a948ad;
    out += quoted_nickname; a948b2..a948e0;
  }
  if (!nickname.empty() && mode==2) return; a948e2..a948ed.
  // With no nickname all three modes use first_name and continue to generated
  // components. A mode other than 0/1/2 ignores nickname and uses first_name.

  W(component) = English WORD form(name.words[component],
                                   name.parts_of_speech[component]);
  C(text) = capitalize ? titlecase(text) : text;
  add_spaced(text): if !out.empty() out+=" "; out+=text;

  // Front/rear compound is joined without an internal separator.
  if ((FrontCompound!=-1 || RearCompound!=-1) &&
      !(shorten && !out.empty())) { a948f3..a9490b;
    compound = W(FrontCompound) + W(RearCompound); a94934/a94948;
    if (!compound.empty()) add_spaced(C(compound)); a9494d..a94995;
  }

  // The exact native gate checks TheX/FirstAdjective/SecondAdjective. A lone
  // HyphenCompound with those three fields all -1 does not enter this group.
  if ((TheX!=-1 || FirstAdjective!=-1 || SecondAdjective!=-1) &&
      !(shorten && !out.empty())) { a949d5..a949f2;
    article_added = false;
    previous_component_needs_space = !out.empty();
    for (component in [FirstAdjective, SecondAdjective, HyphenCompound, TheX]) {
      part = W(component); a94a21/a94ad8/a94b80/a94d05;
      if (part.empty()) continue; // Invalid WORD/POS or empty RAW form.
      if (previous_component_needs_space) out += " ";
      if (!article_added) {
        out += (out.empty() && capitalize) ? "The " : "the ";
        article_added = true; a94a4a..a94a87 (repeated for later first part).
      }
      out += C(part);
      if (component==HyphenCompound) {
        out += "-"; a94c79;
        previous_component_needs_space=false; // TheX follows directly.
      } else previous_component_needs_space=true;
    }
  }
  if (OfX!=-1 && !(shorten && !out.empty())) { a94db2..a94dc6;
    part=W(OfX); a94df3;
    if (!part.empty()) {
      if (!out.empty()) out += " ";
      out += out.empty() ? "Of " : "of "; a94e18..a94e38;
      out += C(part); a94e3d..a94e60;
    }
  }

  Examples of the productive construction, with all fields independently absent:
    {first_name} {front}{rear} the {adjective1} {adjective2} {hyphen}-{noun} of {of_word}
    `{nickname}' {front}{rear} the {adjective1} {noun} of {of_word}  [mode 0]
    {first_name} `{nickname}' {front}{rear} the {noun} of {of_word} [mode 1]
    `{nickname}'                                               [mode 2]
  Without a prior head the initial article is "The "; an OfX-only name begins
  "Of ". With capitalize=false the definite article is always "the ".
  Missing or empty individual fields emit nothing. There is no unknown-name
  fallback, and a named record can yield an empty final string.

ENGLISH WORD/PART-OF-SPEECH FIELD
  reference d2cb50..d2cc1c; classic d29b90..d29c5c; delta -2fc0.
  negative WORD ID, WORD ID >= language.words.size(), or unsigned POS > 8
  returns without appending (d2cb53/d2cb76/d2cb84).
  The 9-entry table d2cc1c selects these language_word offsets:
    0 Noun           +20   d2cb9e
    1 NounPlural     +40   d2cba8
    2 Adjective      +60   d2cbbc
    3 Prefix         +80   d2cbb2
    4 Verb           +a0   d2cbc6
    5 Verb3rdPerson  +c0   d2cbd3
    6 VerbPast       +e0   d2cbe0
    7 VerbPassive    +100  d2cbed
    8 VerbGerund     +120  d2cbfa
  The whole RAW form is appended as one component (d2cc05..d2cc16), so spaces,
  conjunctions and punctuation within it are not independent list boundaries.

NATIVE TITLECASE FIELD
  reference 52d3c0..52d5fe; classic 52ade0..52b01e; delta -25e0.
  This logical body spans several contiguous MSVC unwind records; extraction
  retains it through the sole return and decodes the following tables separately.
  It capitalizes lowercase ASCII at the first ordinary character and at word
  boundaries (52d439..52d509), with these boundaries:
    previous byte is space or double quote;
    previous byte is apostrophe at index 1, or is preceded by a space/comma.
  A '[' increments bracket depth, ']' decrements it; positive depth skips the
  entire enclosed token (52d403..52d430). The first ordinary byte ends the
  initial-boundary state. A backtick is an ordinary byte; the authored nickname
  is not passed through this helper by either name formatter.
  CP437 special mappings use 52d624 remap -> 52d600 RVA table:
    81->9a (ue), a4->a5 (enye), 84->8e (ae umlaut), 86->8f (a ring),
    82->90 (e acute), 94->99 (oe umlaut), 87->80 (c cedilla), 91->92 (ae ligature).
  All other non-ASCII bytes remain unchanged.

UNIT-NAME NICKNAME VARIANTS USED BY THE LIKES SUBJECT
  Unit formatter a94030..a946d1; classic a910b0..a91751; delta -2f80.
  It uses the same has_name, game-type-selected display mode, authored nickname
  punctuation and byte-preserving nickname copy (a9405d..a94187).
  Mode 0 substitutes quoted nickname for first_name and retains generated groups;
  mode 1 places quoted nickname after titlecased first_name and retains groups;
  mode 2 emits quoted nickname alone; absent nickname always retains first_name.
  Its generated groups use the name's local language translation words, rather
  than the English WORD/POS forms: concatenate words[0..1], then words[2..5],
  then words[6], omitting absent entries and separating nonempty groups by spaces.
  Those groups are titlecased; no English "the/of" articles are added here.
  Invalid language/WORD indices contribute no body. This is separate from the
  art-form English grammar above and does not modify user squad.alias values.

WRAPPING/DRAW OWNERSHIP, reference coordinates
  Producer call sites: 1a53ae initial page setup; 1b7c12 selected-tab update.
  Renderer: 17ef01/17ef2c source vector sheet+1a90, 17ef57 boxes sheet+1aa8;
            17f070 calls 858550(box,complete_raw_source), iterating the pair.
  Mouse:    1b791f source+1a90, 1b793e boxes+1aa8 -> 1b79c7 same wrapper.
  Input:    8db31b source.end+1a98, 8db326 source.begin+1a90,
            8db331 boxes+1aa8 -> 8db366 same wrapper.
  Draw:     17f4ad calls ad9790 after reading native text row and its +301 colors.
  These exactly match native_rich_profile.inc's existing Personality ownership;
  Preferences does not require a new capture route or a different native source.
  The full source exists before native word wrapping or justification; any loss
  caused by reconstruction from rendered rows is downstream of this producer.
